page_note: This page is an extended parable/simile about a king and his comitatus on a journey, explicitly applied to the catechumen (ⲡⲕⲁⲧⲏⲭⲟⲩⲙⲉⲛⲟⲥ) and his works. The catechumen is a Manichaean ecclesial category (the lower of the two-tier Elect/Catechumen institutional structure), so the entire teaching unit serves an ecclesial purpose. The simile portion (0-18) does not map cosmos→cosmos; it is a worldly illustration in service of catechumen soteriology. Segments 19-29 make the application explicit. Segment 30 is hortatory ('I have made known to you'). Some substratic vocabulary leaks through ('country of the Living Ones' at seg 29, 'firmaments of the heavens' at seg 23) but woven into the ecclesial frame. Editorial fatigue score elevated (+1.47); damage ratio 60.6%. No discardable formula, but no extractable core teaching either — this is integrated catechumen teaching throughout.
